title: Claimable Shortage of an FBN Inbound Shipment Line
content:
**Calculation.** For Fulfilled by Northloop (FBN), the claimable shortage of a shipment line is the netted shortage of the line, less the over-receipt carry-forward, less the receiving tolerance, less the units already reimbursed as inbound shortage on the same shipment and SKU, each deducted from the netted shortage in that order; a negative remainder counts as zero.

The line is the inbound receipt line of the shipment and SKU named on the seller's open inbound-shortage case.

| Element | Definition |
|---|---|
| Netted shortage | the units expected on that line less the units received on it |
| Over-receipt carry-forward | none |
| Receiving tolerance | the tolerance units of 1 unit plus the tolerance share of 2% (0.02) of the units expected on the line, the share rounded down to a whole unit before it is added |
| Already reimbursed | units on earlier inbound-shortage reimbursements of the same shipment and SKU |

## Worked figures (hypothetical lines)

**Line 1.** Units expected 120, units received 100, 5 units already reimbursed as inbound shortage on that shipment and SKU.
- Netted shortage: 120 less 100, which is 20.
- Receiving tolerance: 2% of 120 is 2.4, rounded down to 2; plus 1 unit, giving 3.
- Claimable shortage: 20 less 0 less 3 less 5, which is **12**.

**Line 2.** Units expected 40, units received 37, nothing reimbursed.
- Netted shortage 3; tolerance 1 plus 2% of 40 (0.8, rounded down to 0), giving 1.
- Claimable shortage: 3 less 0 less 1 less 0, which is **2**.

**Line 3.** Units expected 60, units received 58, 2 units already reimbursed.
- Netted shortage 2; tolerance 1 plus 2% of 60 (1.2, rounded down to 1), giving 2; 2 less 0 less 2 less 2 is below zero, so the claimable shortage is **0**.
